Keep Earth fixed at zero. Keep velocity the same. These choices make the math simpler.

title: Why does more time matter?
text:
**Explain before calculating**

Target R3

Why does more time matter?

A small possible error in velocity adds to the position error each second.

A longer time often gives a wider range of possible positions.

Same possible error, more time

Same uncertain motion, more time. Position (m) versus Time (s). The shaded region is a measurement bound, not a probability.

Central  Lowest possible value  Highest possible value

The shaded range shows possible measurement error. It does not tell how likely a position is.
